submission.natural_language_explanation: N5+ fires on the descriptive, pre-head material of a noun phrase while its head is still ahead: qualitative adjectives in attributive position ('a small stone', 'a famous singer'), attributive nouns inside a compound ('studio album', 'polyimide') and quantity words ('a million dollars'), plus the finite be/do forms that open a predicate complement ('was', 'are'). The same adjectives in predicative position ('the stone is small'), relational/classifying adjectives ('chemical', 'hepatic'), the head noun itself, articles ('a', 'an') and the coordinator 'and' stay at the GELU floor; subword pieces of non-English (Turkish, Chinese, Greek) words also fire, a leftover this reading does not cover.

rival_explanations: Descriptive-register reading: the pole tracks promotional or descriptive prose (product copy, tourism text, reviews) rather than a syntactic modifier slot, so evaluative vocabulary fires anywhere in such text, including in predicative position.

Predicate-opening reading: the pole's real target is the finite verb that opens a predicate (was/are/were) and the first words of its complement, with the attributive-adjective hits a side effect of adjective-rich predicate descriptions.

Core-vocabulary reading: the pole simply fires on tokens outside the model's high-frequency English core (rare words, proper nouns, foreign or technical fragments) regardless of grammatical role, so relational adjectives and technical nouns should fire as readily as 'small' or 'million'.

허가 취소의 전제로 국민건강을 내세웠다. 그동안 얘기하지 않던 안전성과 유효성 문제를 들어 인보사 성분이 바뀐 사실이 국민보건에 위해를 줄 수 있다고 취소 이유를 설명했다.
이런 입장은 최초의 식약처 태도와 상반된 부분이다. 당초 식약처는 코오롱생명과학이 인보사의 성분이 바뀐 것을 고의로 은폐했다고 판단, 이에 초점을 맞췄지만 이번 허가 취소 발표를 하면서는 이전과 달리 고의 은폐 등 도덕성 문제를 전혀 거론하지 않았다.
특히 이런 입장 변화는 향후 이어질 법정 싸움과 관련이 깊다. 고의 은폐에 초점을 맞출 경우 검찰조사와 행정소송 등 코오롱생명과학과 벌여야 할 재판에서 이를 직접 입증해야 하기 때문이다. 다시 말해 보건당국의 대전제인 국민건강이 또 다시 식약처의 책임 회피를 위한 방패막이가 된 셈이다.
식약처는 보건당국의 주체로 이런 문제에 언제나 준비돼 있어야 하며 향후 이와 비슷한 일이 다시 발생하지 않도록, 발생하더라도 명백한 책임을 지고 또 다시 앞으로를 대비해야 한다. 식약처는 이번 일을 뼈저리게 반성하고 교훈을 얻어야 한다는 것, 이점을 반드시 명심하길 바란다.

रोहित शर्मा ने बतौर सलामी बल्लेबाज आईपीएल में छक्कों का दोहरा शतक पूरा कर लिया. रोहित शर्मा आईपीएल में 200 छक्के लगाने वाले चौथे बल्लेबाज बन गए. रोहित शर्मा ने 190 मैचों में 200 छक्के लगाए हैं. आईपीएल में रोहित शर्मा के 4990 रन हो गए. हालांकि वह 5000 रन पूरा करने से 10 रन दूर रह गए. लेकिन अगले मैच में रोहित शर्मा यह रिकॉर्ड अपने नाम कर लेंगे.

Coffee grounds and coffee filters are good nitrogen sources ('greens') in a compost pile, so add as part of the greens in your compost pile.
Coffee grounds can also be used as a mulch. They are acidic and can be used as a mulch by themselves around evergreens, camellias, and other acid loving plants.
If you have a worm bin of red wigglers, use coffee grounds as worm food. Worms love coffee grounds, and the grounds enhance the texture of the final compost. Tea leaves, tea bags (be sure to remove staples) and coffee filters are also acceptable worm food. Earthworms love coffee grounds too, so using as a mulch and/or in the compost pile is attractive to them as well.

You can add any organic matter you choose. Spread your organic matter on top of the soil. Here's where the manual labor comes in. The organic matter needs to be mixed into the top six to twelve inches of soil. Digging it in and mixing it with a shovel is a great way to do this, as it moves a lot of earth without pulverizing the soil particles the way tilling can. However, if digging is just too hard on your back, using a tiller is a fine method.
When you're finished, your garden bed will be several inches higher than it was originally. It will settle some over the course of a season, but the soil structure will keep improving as microorganisms in the soil work to break down all of the organic matter you've added. The bed can be planted immediately, however. You'll be adding more organic matter on the top of the bed as a mulch once or twice a year. This will continue the process of improving soil structure and offset any settling that happens.
It is more difficult to improve soil around trees and other established plants than unplanted soil in, for example, a vegetable bed. To improve the fertility and the structure of the soil, consider using a thin (1 to 2 inch) layer of compost as mulch around the drip line of the tree or plant. Mulch is used on top of the existing soil surface.
Be careful not to cultivate the soil (dig in) around the tree or plant, since many feeder roots are near the surface and cultivation can harm them. The compost mulch can be reapplied as needed.

You can also refresh a pot by thoroughly mixing in about one-third by volume of new potting soil and adding fertilizer.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The stone is small and grey, worn smooth by the river.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The hypothesis's own predicative floor example ('the stone is small') with predicative qualitative adjectives, so it predicts silence even though a copula is present, while the register and predicate-opening rivals predict a hit.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Critics call the singer famous across Europe but she rarely gives interviews.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Object-complement predicative 'famous' with no attributive modifier: the hypothesis predicts the floor, the register rival reads review prose as active, and the predicate rival sees no finite be/do form.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The room felt large and empty after they removed the furniture.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Predicative qualitative adjectives after the linking verb 'felt' with no be/do form, so the hypothesis and the predicate-opening rival predict silence while the register rival fires on the evaluative description.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She found the lecture dull but the seminar useful.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Predicative adjectives in object-complement position ('found the lecture dull') are outside the claimed attributive slot, so the hypothesis predicts silence while the register rival reads the evaluative vocabulary as a hit.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Though small, quiet and cheap, the flat suited them.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Fronted predicative adjectives ('small, quiet and cheap') sit before the noun but outside its phrase, so the hypothesis predicts no pre-head modifier firing while the register rival fires on the evaluative description.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The hepatic unit handles transplants and referrals.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Relational adjective 'hepatic' in attributive position is a named inactive class for the hypothesis, but the core-vocabulary rival fires on the technical word.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The pattern looked pulmonary on the scan.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Relational adjective 'pulmonary' in predicative position after the linking verb 'looked', which the hypothesis predicts stays at the floor, while the core-vocabulary rival fires on the technical word.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She wanted something beautiful for the wall.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Claimed trigger 'beautiful' in postnominal position after the head 'something', not pre-head while the head is ahead, so the hypothesis predicts silence and no rival has a reason to fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The chemical leaked from a drum in the storeroom.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The named word 'chemical' used as a head noun rather than an attributive relational adjective, which the hypothesis's head-noun class predicts is silent, while the role-blind core-vocabulary rival still fires on the relational-adjective word.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: They cured the polyimide overnight in the laboratory.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Here 'polyimide' is the head noun of its phrase rather than the modifier in a compound, which the hypothesis predicts is at the floor, while the core-vocabulary rival fires on the rare technical token regardless of role.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The garden looked beautiful after the rain.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Claimed trigger 'beautiful' in predicative position after the linking verb 'looked' rather than before a noun head, which the hypothesis predicts is silent while the register rival fires on the evaluative description.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The album leaked online before its release.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Head noun 'album' with no attributive material, which the hypothesis's 'head noun itself' class predicts is silent.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: An engineer and an architect met at an exhibition.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Articles ('An', 'an', 'an') plus the coordinator 'and' with only head nouns, combining two named inactive classes in one probe.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The suspect remained at large until the spring.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Claimed trigger 'large' appears in the predicative idiom 'at large', which the hypothesis's predicative-position class predicts stays at the floor.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The table and the chairs stood in the corridor.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The coordinator 'and' joining two definite head nouns with no modifier or be/do form, the hypothesis's named inactive coordinator class.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: It took time to finish the report before the deadline.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Claimed trigger token 'time' appears as the head of its noun phrase ('all-time' was the activating context), which the hypothesis's head-noun class predicts is silent.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The roof of the house leaks whenever it rains.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Claimed trigger token 'of' in a plain partitive phrase with no pre-head descriptive material, testing the token in a context the hypothesis does not cover.

adversarial_test_results.detail: Claimed trigger token 'but' used mid-sentence between two verbs in a sentence with only articles, head nouns and lexical verbs.

readings.explanation: N5+ fires on the descriptive, pre-head material of a noun phrase while its head is still ahead: qualitative adjectives in attributive position ('a small stone', 'a famous singer'), attributive nouns inside a compound ('studio album', 'polyimide') and quantity words ('a million dollars'), plus the finite be/do forms that open a predicate complement ('was', 'are'). The same adjectives in predicative position ('the stone is small'), relational/classifying adjectives ('chemical', 'hepatic'), the head noun itself, articles ('a', 'an') and the coordinator 'and' stay at the GELU floor; subword pieces of non-English (Turkish, Chinese, Greek) words also fire, a leftover this reading does not cover.

Descriptive-register reading: the pole tracks promotional or descriptive prose (product copy, tourism text, reviews) rather than a syntactic modifier slot, so evaluative vocabulary fires anywhere in such text, including in predicative position.

Predicate-opening reading: the pole's real target is the finite verb that opens a predicate (was/are/were) and the first words of its complement, with the attributive-adjective hits a side effect of adjective-rich predicate descriptions.

Core-vocabulary reading: the pole simply fires on tokens outside the model's high-frequency English core (rare words, proper nouns, foreign or technical fragments) regardless of grammatical role, so relational adjectives and technical nouns should fire as readily as 'small' or 'million'.
